 That's all for this game - thanks a lot for joining us.
 This result sets us up nicely for our second game of the day, which sees London City Lionesses host Crystal Palace.
 Victory for the hosts would move them up to 23 points, four behind Chelsea.
 Do join us for that one from 16:30 GMT.
 If you can't make it, then we'll have five games tomorrow afternoon. Lovely stuff!
 Image source, Getty Images

 'Really stuck to the task' - Taylor published at 15:07 GMT 15:07 GMT 
 FT: Liverpool 0-0 Chelsea 
 Liverpool 
 Liverpool manager Gareth Taylor: "I am really pleased. The girls stuck to the game plan phenomenally well against a tough opponent and I cannot give them enough credit for what they did today. A lot of top individual performances and as a collective we really stuck to the task.
 "They had some chances, we had some chances - ours were probably better. And then in the second half, we didn't have the same amount because it's fatiguing to replicate that pressure and at times we didn't keep the ball well enough. But credit to the players. I am so pleased they held on as sometimes you need that just for all your work.
 "Grace Fisk has defended half the pitch against [Alyssa] Thompson and she was outstanding. We can't do what we want to do without Fisky. When they got through, Khiara was there to make the saves.
 "Performances have been good in general and it's good now the players are starting to take some reward for their endeavours. We want to continue to push and improve. It's a really competitive WSL and there are no easy games."

 Where is ABJ going to get any confidence from?! Unlikely to see minutes for England and Lola Brown (who was probably Chelsea's best player) coming on before her.
 Ed, Plymouth 
 Beever Jones should have started to give some height to their attack, especially for corners. Substitutions should have been made much sooner. Cuthbert introduced sooner, for a must-win game, to stay top of the table? Just handed the lead back to Manchester City! Very disappointing after last week's great result.
 Paul, Canada 
 5 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Missing being clinical' - Bompastor published at 15:02 GMT 15:02 GMT 
 FT: Liverpool 0-0 Chelsea 
 Chelsea 
 Chelsea manager Sonia Bompastor: "Of course, it's frustrating when we are not able to get the three points. It was really good we didn't concede any goals, we are really strong, but when you want to win, you need to figure out how to score goals. Today the quality was not as I would have liked to break down this team.
 "Coming at the end of this block, the bodies and heads were a little tired and the energy not as high as we would have liked but we still had the quality to be able to bring the three points. In the second half we were dominant, but what we are missing is being clinical and ruthless in the box.
 "Having all squad available always a big help. But we work with the players on the pitch and we had enough quality to win this game with the players that were there."

 She was pipped to the player of the match award by her captain, but how good was Liverpool goalkeeper Khiara Keating today?
 Keating made seven saves, several of them superb, to secure a second clean sheet on the bounce.
 Liverpool have kept a clean sheet in four of their 11 WSL games this term; only Chelsea (7) have done this more often in the Women's Super League this season.
 Image source, Getty Images

 Post published at 14:45 GMT 14:45 GMT 
 FT: Liverpool 0-0 Chelsea 
 Liverpool 
 Liverpool captain and player of the match Grace Fisk speaking to Sky Sports: "It was a really tough game, second half especially. We didn't have as much of the ball as we would have hoped. It was a lot of last-ditch defending and Khiara made some incredible saves.
 "We didn't want to sit deep but sometimes it works out like that. To take points off the league leaders is something to be proud of. Some of her [Keating's] saves were unbelievable today.
 "We have had a tough start, but today showed how good we can be and what we are capable of."
 Liverpool goalkeeper Khiara Keating: "It was a bit stressful; we don't want to sit back but in games like this you have to ride it out.
 "clean sheet is always on our minds every game; we knew the mission. It was such a close game, it could have gone either way."

 By Joe Bradshaw BBC Sport senior journalist Chelsea missed the chance to consolidate their lead over Manchester City at the top of the Women's Super League as they failed to breach stubborn Liverpool at a sunny St Helen's Stadium. 
 After beating the champions impressively at Stamford Bridge last week, Blues boss Sonia Bompastor named a starting XI without a recognised striker only to see her side denied by a fine performance from home goalkeeper Khiara Keating. 
 The ex-Manchester City stopper produced fine saves from Alyssa Thompson, Wieke Kaptein and Sandy Baltimore before diving to turn Sjoeke Nusken's second-half volley aside.
 This lack of clinical edge highlighted the league leaders' limitations at the top of the pitch with first-choice forward Melvine Malard sidelined until the new year through injury and out-of-form Aggie Beever-Jones left on the bench until the 83rd minute.
 Liverpool had been excellent in the first half, going close through Vivien Endemann and Fuka Nagano, but they faded in the face of relentless Chelsea pressure.
 Yet Keating held firm, making seven saves in total and ensuring their unbeaten visitors slipped to a third draw of the season.
 There will be smiles at her old club City too as this result means they can return to the summit if they win their game in hand at home to Tottenham on Sunday (12:00 GMT).
 Analysis: Chelsea's attack exposed in frustrating draw 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Chelsea had 69% possession and 47 touches inside the Liverpool penalty area but could not score
 Chelsea's title challenge this season has been built on an outstanding defence, with this a seventh clean sheet in 12 games and their five goals conceded comfortably the best record in the WSL.
 Hannah Hampton was required to make some routine saves in the first half but generally they kept the persistent hosts at arm's length.
 It is the other end of the pitch that will concern Bompastor.
 Summer signing Malard had scored six in six games before suffering a hamstring injury against Manchester City and in her absence they could not get the vital breakthrough.
 Fielding wide forward Thompson as a number nine did not work against rugged home captain Grace Fisk, although they created enough in a dominant second half to feel they should have won.
 Nineteen shots, seven on target and an expected goals (xG) of 1.92 reflected that, but Keating proved impregnable.
 With a three-week break for international football after this weekend, the Blues will have plenty of time to stew on a frustrating draw. They face third-placed London City Lionesses next on Saturday, 12 December.
 However, this result will encourage Liverpool, who have run both Manchester City and Arsenal close so far this season. Here, they got the point their determined defending warranted.
 Indeed, they could have snatched all three on the break in injury time had Beata Olsson not flashed a late effort wide.
